wave.notes: truth: functions = dtk symbols.txt entries with type:function (stripped excluded), start/size from the symbol; verified=1 iff the function lies in a splits.txt unit whose configure.py Object(...) status evaluates to Matching (configure.py executed for this version; NonMatching/Equivalent/missing units and code outside any named unit => 0). linked_percent = verified function bytes / all listed function bytes (bytes, all modules). REL address convention: a REL has no addresses of its own; each REL section i is placed as romwright's REL loader does. placement=disc-sequential: RELs that are plain files on the disc are imported together with the DOL from the disc image; modules in module-id order, sections in table order from the load base (dol::rel_base, = dtk 'rel merge' layout), each section 32-byte aligned, empty sections skipped; load_address = lowest sized section. placement=standalone-windows: RELs packed inside an archive (RARC/U8) that the disc importer does not open; imported standalone, section i (REL section-table index) at 0x80000000 + i*0x10000000; load_address = lowest sized section. tsv start = section base + dtk section-relative symbol offset (REL splits/symbols list sections in REL section order, sized sections only). Rev 0 disc; DOL and all RELs hash-checked against config.yml. 415 RELs: 235 are plain files under files/rels/ (found by the disc importer), 180 are Yaz0-packed inside files/RELS.arc (RARC rels/amem, rels/mmem) which the importer does not open (blocker: RARC members not linked from disc). disc importer links 235 of 415 RELs (others: archive members or duplicate REL module ids, which the importer skips) . Import: ISO import links the 235 plain files/rels/*.rel (151077 relocations applied); the 180 RELs inside files/RELS.arc (RARC, Yaz0 members) are NOT linked: importer blocker, no RARC support in disc.rs (is_rel_name only matches FST files). Those are imported standalone (windows convention). Truth start recall vs importer: main 13604/13754, linked RELs 16855/16980.

wave.source_archive: Minerva_Myrient/No-Intro/Nintendo - Nintendo 64 (BigEndian)/Legend of Zelda, The - Ocarina of Time (USA).zip
wave.notes: Compression: Yaz0 for `code` and every actor/gamestate overlay; `makerom` entry and `boot` are raw. main = entrypoint(0x80000400) + boot (0x80000460, ROM 0x1060) + code (0x800110a0, Yaz0 at ROM 0xa62840). 469 overlay modules (ovl_*, n64dd) at the vram they are linked at in the build (the dmadata/ActorOverlay link address; the ROM overlay bytes equal the ELF section bytes byte-for-byte, relocation table follows the code in the decoded file). Sizes come from the IDO .mdebug stEnd records (compiler truth, no padding) plus ELF symtab for 56 asm functions. sha1 not published by the repo (md5 only). Import mapping (romwright N64): native/n64.rs maps ROM[0x1000..] linearly at the header boot address (word 0x08) plus the whole ROM at 0x10000000; only a ROM whose header CRC1/CRC2/game code is in native/n64_layouts.json (today only Perfect Dark NTSC-final) is loaded as real segments through native/n64_segments.rs (each segment = ROM parts decoded by n64_codec [raw, deflate, rare-1172/1173/-pages, mio0, yay0, yaz0], placed at boot/at/after; two segments may not overlap in RDRAM). Overlays are placed by native/n64_overlays.rs import_set(rom, [(name, rom_offset, codec, load_address, stored size)]): one NativeImport per overlay, mapped at its load address, module kind overlay. functions.tsv `start` is the VRAM link address of the decoded segment/overlay (module=main: resident segments, one address space; any other module: its own program at its load_address, so overlays sharing a vram never collide). truth/layout.json lists every resident segment and overlay (ROM range, codec, vram, decoded size) in n64_layouts.json schema so a harness can build Layout/import_set input; it is NOT in the shipped catalog, so a stock romwright import of this ROM is the linear view and only `linear_visible` main functions line up.
